rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify ADVERSE ICFR opinion in same KPMG attestation report. Mode B — derive: revenue-recognition control failure + inventory valuation control failure together cover the two highest-risk audit assertions; question whether the 'no identified material misstatements' management assurance is auditor-corroborated.

rfm_tuples.M_value: AUDITOR_CHANGE signal=CLEAN_BIG4_TENURE (KPMG, Big 4, no resignation/disagreement language). Progress narrative is credible (pervasive MWs narrowed to three discrete process-level MWs) but the remaining MWs are not low-risk peripheral controls — they sit directly on revenue completeness and inventory valuation. KPMG's continued engagement and clean financial-statement opinion reduce fraud-tail risk; this is process-quality distress, not accounting-quality distress.

rfm_tuples.R: 'During the year ended December 31, 2023, AdaptHealth experienced declines in its market capitalization as a result of a sustained decrease in AdaptHealth's stock price and also revised its financial projections. AdaptHealth considered these items to represent triggering events and performed a goodwill impairment test at each quarterly reporting date during 2023. Based on the results of the tests performed as of September 30, 2023 and December 31, 2023, ... AdaptHealth recognized an aggregate non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $830.8 million during the year ended December 31, 2023.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify timing and magnitude vs Q3'23 10-Q. Mode B — derive: management revised projections downward — what specifically changed in the projections that the MD&A does not quantify? Compare cumulative impairment to acquisition history (single reporting unit) to assess M&A-overpayment exposure.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q3'23 10-Q discloses $511.866M goodwill impairment at Sept 30 2023 (verified). Q4'23 incremental impairment ≈ $830.8M − $511.9M = $318.9M (about 62% of Q3 charge in a single additional quarter). Total $830.8M = 26% of 2023 net revenue ($3.20B). Goodwill remained on balance sheet despite impairment — implies pre-charge goodwill was ~$2.0B+ from SPAC-era acquisition history (DFB Healthcare 2019 + AeroCare 2021 + diabetes deals). Two-step impairment in two consecutive quarters indicates projections were revised DOWN in Q4 after the Q3 impairment had already booked the then-current view — i.e., the Q3 valuation was already stale within one quarter.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Sequential quarterly impairment (Q3 then Q4) is a serial-write-down pattern, indicating management's projection model was overly optimistic at Q3 and had to be reset again three months later. The MD&A does not quantify which assumptions (revenue growth, discount rate, control premium) drove the second leg — that opacity is a Mode-B finding. The $830.8M total wipes out approximately the entire 2019-2021 acquisition premium and implicitly admits the AeroCare-era M&A strategy destroyed value. Forensic priority signal.

rfm_tuples.R: 'AdaptHealth was in compliance with the applicable covenants in the aforementioned credit facility as of December 31, 2023.' + 'At December 31, 2023, based on the financial debt covenants under the 2021 Credit Agreement, the maximum amount the Company could borrow under the 2021 Revolver and remain in compliance with the financial debt covenants under the agreement was $226.2 million.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify revolver headroom math. Mode B — derive: $226.2M of $450M revolver = 50.3% capacity is covenant-blocked even though current draw is $0 — implies the Consolidated Total Leverage Ratio covenant is binding at present pro-forma, not theoretical.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Revolver commitment: $450M. Outstanding at YE2023: $0. Covenant-allowed maximum incremental draw: $226.2M (50.3% of facility). Therefore $223.8M (49.7%) of nominal revolver capacity is INACCESSIBLE due to covenant constraints — this is the true measure of liquidity headroom. Q1'24 10-Q shows the company drew $75M of revolver in Q1'24 (revolver balance moved from $0 -> $75M) while paying down $25M of term loan, net debt rose +$50M. Term Loan outstanding $720M (YE23) -> $695M (Q1'24). Total debt maturity wall: $626.6M in 2026 (revolver + term loan maturity). No covenant amendments disclosed in either filing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: 'In compliance' present-tense statement obscures that the company is in compliance with ~50% covenant cushion on the revolver. Combined with the Q1'24 draw, the trajectory is toward tighter headroom, not looser. Unlike AAP-style distressed credits, AHCO has NOT yet amended covenants — but the company is approaching the 2026 maturity wall with the leverage ratio already pinching new borrowing capacity. Refinancing risk is real but not imminent.

The Sleep segment grew 16.4% ($1.241B vs $1.067B), Respiratory grew 7.9% ($598.8M vs $555.0M). Diabetes segment DECLINED 3.9% ($660.0M vs $687.1M). rfm_tuples.M_value: Operational metrics IMPROVING, not deteriorating: Adj EBITDA margin 21.0% > 20.0%; total revenue +7.7%; Q1'24 operating income +93%. Diabetes decline (-3.9%) is the only segment soft spot; the 10-K names GLP-1 agonists (Mounjaro/Wegovy/Ozempic) as a risk factor that 'may have a significant impact on obesity rates over time, which may result in reduced demand for our current equipment.' rfm_tuples.interpretation: Strongest counter-narrative signal: the underlying business is COMPOUNDING. A forensic analyst applying the honesty-alpha framework should note this is a 'badly priced equity, not lying management' setup — re-detecting goodwill write-downs is not alpha, but identifying that the impairment was NOT accompanied by EBITDA/cash deterioration IS a Mode-B catch.

Senior notes coupons are well below current market rates (4.625%/5.125% vs current 7-9% for similar BB credits), so refinancing the 2026 secured debt will likely materially raise interest expense. Interest expense rose from $111M (2022) to $134M (2023) already; refinancing $1.17B at +200-300bp would add $20-35M annually to interest expense, compressing the interest-coverage covenant.

Combined with the covenant-cushion finding in C3 (only 50% revolver headroom), the path to early-2026 either requires (a) Adj EBITDA growth to widen leverage cushion, (b) asset divestitures, or (c) equity issuance. summary: AHCO is a pre-cutoff drawdown name where the SEVERITY of the surface disclosures (ADVERSE ICFR opinion second year running, $830.8M sequential goodwill impairment, interim CEO, $51M securities class action) is real but the underlying operating trajectory is COMPOUNDING (Adj EBITDA +11.7%, margin expansion, Q1'24 operating income +93%, Sleep segment +16.4% — Philips recall tailwind). Two major overhangs visibly resolving before cutoff: permanent CEO announced April 17 2024 effective May 20 2024 (pre-cutoff), and class-action settlement Stipulation entered Jan 17 2024 with $17.8M already in escrow by Q1'24. Insider Form 4 register shows ~$35.7M of selling concentrated in early 2023 (before goodwill impairment) and zero insider purchases, which is a moderate negative but consistent with 10%+ holders unwinding rather than active fraud. Refinancing risk is the live forward issue: $626.6M maturity wall in January 2026 with revolver headroom already covenant-blocked at ~50%. Net read: this is a 'distressed price, healthy operations' setup where the forensic framework's exclusion-of-liars discipline catches that AHCO is NOT lying about deterioration — the operations are genuinely recovering. LONG-tier on the honesty-alpha basis, with the caveat that 2026 refi remains a real binary.
